title: onboard-diagnostic-decision-brief-aug-2027
body:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the contrastive onboarding tournament we ran for candidate model family 'Acadia-v2' variants (fp16 / int8-ggml / q4_ktd) across three production workloads: consumer-chat, short-form summarization, and semantic-search. The goal: pick a primary serving variant for Hosted API with a fallback strategy that preserves latency SLOs and minimizes observed quality regressions vs baseline Acadia-v1.

Executive summary (short):
- Winner by adjusted quality score: Acadia-v2-fp16 (Elo-like score 1683).
- Best cost/latency tradeoff without >3% quality regression: Acadia-v2-q4_ktd (Elo-like 1621) — recommended for Dedicated burst pool trials.
- int8-ggml showed large variance on long-context QA prompts; high failure modes on entity hallucination -> do not promote to hosted baseline.
- Action: promote Acadia-v2-fp16 to canary for Hosted API (5% traffic) with tight regressions monitoring for two prompt cohorts (legal & financial). Start Dedicated burst pilot with q4_ktd in staging.

Notes on uniqueness of this run:
- We used a contrastive tournament (round-robin + transitive scoring) rather than a single-lift leaderboard, to better surface pairwise contradictions across prompt families.
- Introduced a small synthetic adversary promptset (edge-synth-45) to highlight hallucination and instruction-drift risks not visible in default eval sets.
- We computed an adjusted score that penalizes variance across prompts (stability penalty) so the result favors more predictable variants.

Evaluation setup (short):
- Candidates: Acadia-v1 (baseline), Acadia-v2-fp16, Acadia-v2-q4_ktd, Acadia-v2-int8-ggml, Acadia-v2-fp16-lr2 (aggressive top-k tweak).
- Workloads: consumer-chat (CC), short-summary (SS), semantic-search (SSearch).
- Prompt families: polite-dialogue, instruction-follow, long-context-QA, multi-step-reasoning, edge-synth-45 (synthetic stress).
- Metrics: quality_score (human-calibrated composite from 0-100), failure_rate (explicit hallucination or unsafe output), latency_p95 (ms), tokens_per_sec, cost_est (tokens * unit_cost_est).
- Pairwise methodology: sample 2,500 prompts per family, run head-to-head comparisons with blind human raters for ambiguous wins; compute win/loss/tie counts and transform to Elo-like scores with stability penalty = 1/(1+stddev_per_prompt_family).

Leaderboard (adjusted scores, higher better):
1) Acadia-v2-fp16 — 1683 
   - quality_score: 86.1, failure_rate: 1.8%, latency_p95: 84ms, est_unit_cost: 1.00x
2) Acadia-v2-q4_ktd — 1621
   - quality_score: 82.7, failure_rate: 2.4%, latency_p95: 62ms, est_unit_cost: 0.42x
3) Acadia-v2-fp16-lr2 — 1599
   - quality_score: 81.9, failure_rate: 2.1%, latency_p95: 92ms, est_unit_cost: 1.05x
4) Acadia-v1 (baseline) — 1570
   - quality_score: 80.8, failure_rate: 2.6%, latency_p95: 88ms, est_unit_cost: 1.00x
5) Acadia-v2-int8-ggml — 1454
   - quality_score: 75.3, failure_rate: 6.9%, latency_p95: 48ms, est_unit_cost: 0.28x

Pairwise win/loss highlights (headlines):
- fp16 beat q4_ktd on long-context-QA by 9.7% absolute win rate.
- q4_ktd beat fp16 on instruction-follow (short prompts) by 6.1% absolute win rate, primarily due to faster finish and fewer truncations.
- int8-ggml lost to baseline Acadia-v1 on multi-step-reasoning in 68% of sampled comparisons (systematic omission of intermediate steps).
- fp16-lr2 produced higher verbosity, which sometimes improved quality_score but raised failure_rate on safety-sensitive prompts.

Win/Loss matrix (pairwise % wins when A vs B):
- Acadia-v2-fp16 vs Acadia-v2-q4_ktd: fp16 wins 54.9%, ties 23.4%, q4_ktd wins 21.7%
- Acadia-v2-fp16 vs Acadia-v1: fp16 wins 58.2%, ties 19.8%, baseline wins 22.0%
- Acadia-v2-q4_ktd vs Acadia-v1: q4_ktd wins 46.5%, ties 27.3%, baseline wins 26.2%
- Acadia-v2-int8-ggml vs Acadia-v1: int8 wins 29.6%, ties 18.0%, baseline wins 52.4%

Per-workload deltas (relative quality_score change vs baseline Acadia-v1):
- Consumer-chat: fp16 +3.2, q4_ktd +1.6, int8 -4.9
- Short-summary: fp16 +2.7, q4_ktd +2.1, int8 -2.3
- Semantic-search: fp16 +1.9, q4_ktd +3.5, int8 -1.1

Regression findings (notable):
1) Safety-sensitive prompts (legal / financial): fp16 shows small but measurable increase in hallucination rate on citation-style prompts (from 0.4% to 0.9%). This is borderline for hosted promotion and will be part of the canary gating.
2) Long-context QA: int8-ggml systematically omits chain-of-thought like steps when prompts exceed ~1,500 tokens. Failure modes include truncated reasoning and confident-but-wrong final answers.
3) Adversarial synthetic set (edge-synth-45): q4_ktd has fewer hallucinations than int8 but more format-violations (missing bullets/JSON keys) compared to fp16.
4) Latency anomalies: fp16-lr2 had three observed tail spikes tied to its top-k sampling knob interacting with batching; reproducible on small batches (1-4).

Qualitative examples (short):
- Long-context-QA example where int8-ggml fails: prompt with nested facts; int8 returns a plausible but incorrect entity with high confidence.
- Instruction-follow where q4_ktd excels: very short 'convert this to a haiku' prompts — q4_ktd often returns tighter, less verbose outputs and nabs higher human preference for concision.

Cost/latency tradeoff table (selection):
- fp16: baseline cost multiplier 1.0, predictable latency, best raw quality.
- q4_ktd: ~0.4x cost, 25-35% lower p95 latency, slightly lower but stable quality for short prompts.
- int8-ggml: ~0.28x cost, best p95 for tiny batches, but large quality variance on long prompts — high-risk for Hosted.

Decision recommendation (detailed):
1) Hosted API primary: Acadia-v2-fp16 — canary 5% global traffic for 14 days. Gating rules: no more than +0.6% absolute increase in safety hallucination rate on legal/financial prompt cohort, and no >1.5% drop in human-calibrated composite quality in A/B sample relative to baseline. If either fails, rollback to Acadia-v1 and open incident review.
2) Dedicated trial: Acadia-v2-q4_ktd — run a 2-week dedicated pilot on a reserved burst pool for production partners who opt-in. Monitor latency_p95, cost, and user-reported correctness. If pilot shows <2% delta in core quality for short-form workloads, expand to additional customers.
3) int8-ggml: do not promote to Hosted; instead, put into 'research-mode' for targeted optimization (quantization-aware finetuning and long-context stress tests).
4) fp16-lr2: hold for now; investigate and fix top-k/batching tail interactions before wider rollout.

Monitoring & rollout plan (practical):
- Canary dashboard: add two cohorts (legal/financial prompt cohort; long-context QA cohort) with continuous sampling, automated human-in-the-loop rechecks for any alert, and a daily summary email to eng-applied-ml and product-hosted-api.
- Automated regression alerts: threshold-based on composite quality (-1.0 point), failure_rate (+0.6% absolute), and latency (+20ms p95).
- Shadow runs: run q4_ktd in shadow for 10% of Dedicated traffic to validate cost numbers in production.

Open risks and mitigation:
- Risk: subtle instruction drift in fp16 variants triggered by recent weights pruning during training. Mitigation: enable periodic calibration with a 500-item curated promptset and block promotion if drift exceeds thresholds.
- Risk: int8 exposure to long-context tasks leads to scaled user impact if accidentally routed. Mitigation: tag models and routing policies to prevent fallbacks to int8 for long-context routes.

Next steps & action items:
- (Rohit) Create canary rollout changelist and schedule for Aug 20, 2027.
- (Priya) Wire up the two special prompt cohorts into the canary dashboard by Aug 18.
- (Dmitri) Run targeted quant-aware training experiment for int8-ggml and report by Sep 3.
- (Sara) Add safety-calibration prompts to the nightly eval harness and enable automated gating checks.
- (Marta) Draft customer-facing note for Dedicated pilot opt-in and ROI expectations (due Aug 19).

Appendix (short):
- Full raw head-to-head matrices, raw human ratings, and per-example failure annotations are attached in JIRA-ML-2247.
- Quick scripts used: github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/tree/main/tournaments/contrastive-run (PR #612).

If reviewers want a live walkthrough, I'll prepare a 30-minute session next week (Aug 18 or 19) to step through the canary dashboard and sample failure cases.
